readerTitle: Ten customers in four months: a bookkeeper's first sales
caseNote: 가상 시뮬레이션 (배관·냉난방 업체 대상 기장 대행 서비스) · 모든 인물과 수치는 설명용
insight: 첫 고객 10명은 마케팅이 아니라 창업자가 고른 판단 네 가지로 만들어진다. 누구에게, 어떻게 다가가고, 얼마를 받고, 거절에서 무엇을 배우느냐가 그것이다.
misconception: 첫 고객은 최대한 넓게 알리고, 무료나 큰 할인으로 일단 많이 모으면 된다.

sources.text: 모든 인물, 가격, 수치는 설명용 가상 예시
이 유닛(SAL-06)의 개념 레슨: 첫 고객 10명, 콜드 아웃리치, 디자인 파트너, 첫 거래 가격, 실패한 거래에서 배우기

factChecks.note: 모든 수치는 가상입니다. 6번 카드 퍼널 검산: 대화 60명 → 상담 17명 → 유료 고객 10명, 이 중 소개로 온 고객 6명. 17명 중 10명 전환(약 59%), 고객 10명 중 6명이 소개라는 점이 서로 모순되지 않는지 확인했습니다.
가격 검산: 정가 월 $400, 창립 고객 가격 월 $300(25% 할인), 6개월 한정. 6개월간 할인액은 고객당 $600입니다.
배관 자재상(supply house)에서 아침 일찍 업주를 만나는 장면은 업계 관행에 기댄 설명용 설정입니다. 특정 국가나 지역의 사실로 서술하지 않았습니다.

cards.title: Ten customers in four months: a bookkeeper's first sales
body: Dana spent eight years at an accounting firm. Now she has her own bookkeeping service, a laptop, and a monthly price of $400. She has zero customers.
Over the next four months you make her four key sales decisions. Each one changes what happens next.

image.label: A bookkeeper at a kitchen table with a laptop and an empty client list
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 부엌 식탁에 노트북, 커피, 빈칸 10개가 있는 고객 명단 메모지. 창밖은 이른 아침. 실제 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Who should Dana go after first?
body: Dana's old clients included many trades businesses. She knows their books are often months behind. But almost every small business needs a bookkeeper.
Where should she aim her first month of selling?

options.text: Any small business in the city. The bigger the pool, the more leads
options.feedback: More names, but a vague pitch. A café and a law office have different problems, so every conversation starts from zero.

options.text: Plumbing and heating firms with 2–10 staff whose books are behind
options.feedback: Same pain, same words, same places to find them. These owners also talk to each other, so one happy customer can lead to the next.

options.text: Larger firms with 50+ staff, for bigger monthly fees
options.feedback: Each deal is worth more, but they often have an accountant already and take months to decide. Dana needs quick lessons now.

cards.title: Say you chose plumbing and heating firms. How does Dana reach them?
body: These owners spend their days on job sites, not reading email. Dana has a little money and a lot of time.

image.label: Tradespeople at a supply counter early in the morning
image.brief: 새벽 배관 자재상 카운터. 작업복 차림의 업주들이 부품을 받는 사이, 한 여성이 커피를 들고 짧게 대화 중. 따뜻한 조명. 실제 브랜드나 로고 없음.

options.text: Buy a list and send 500 emails
options.feedback: Cheap and fast. But busy owners skip it, and the few replies won't tell her why the rest ignored her.

options.text: Ask old clients for introductions, and visit the local supply house at 7 a.m. to talk to owners in person
options.feedback: Slow and tiring, but each conversation teaches her which words land. A warm introduction also comes with trust built in.

options.text: Build a website and run local ads
options.feedback: This helps later. Right now Dana doesn't know which promise makes an owner act, so the ads would be guesses.

cards.title: Say you went in person. Then Luis says: "I'll try it if it's free."
body: Luis runs a six-person plumbing firm. His books are four months behind. He likes Dana but isn't sure the service is worth $400 a month.

options.text: Do it free for three months to win him over
options.feedback: She gets a customer, but no proof anyone will pay. Free customers also give politer, less useful feedback.
It protects her price, but she may lose a willing first customer and everything he could teach her.

options.text: Offer $300 for six months if he joins a 20-minute feedback call each month and refers two owners if he's happy
options.feedback: Luis pays real money and becomes a partner in shaping the service. The discount buys something specific and has an end date.

cards.title: Say Luis signed. By week six, a customer walks away.
body: Dana has four paying customers. Then Priya, who runs a heating firm, ends her trial month and says no thanks.

options.text: Thank her and move on. There are plenty of other owners
options.feedback: It saves time and pride, but she loses the cheapest lesson she'll get. The next Priya may leave for the same reason.
It might keep her. But if price wasn't the reason, Dana just cut her revenue and learned nothing.

options.text: Ask for 15 minutes to hear exactly why
options.feedback: Priya explains that her monthly reports arrived too late to price new jobs. Dana moves every customer's report to the 5th of the month.

cards.title: Ten customers, and where they came from.
body: Most of her customers came from introductions, not from cold contact. Two of the referrals came from Luis, as agreed. The earlier reports also gave her a sharper pitch: "Know your numbers before you quote the next job."

breakdown.label: Trial conversations
breakdown.detail: Owners who looked at their own books with her

breakdown.label: Paying customers
breakdown.detail: Including Luis, at a founding price

cards.title: What got Dana here won't get her to 100.
body: Morning visits, personal calls and custom deals took most of her week. That's fine for ten customers. It's not a plan for a hundred.

The first ten also tell you about the first ten. They chose to take a chance on a newcomer, and later customers may be more careful. And keep feedback in proportion: one loud customer shouldn't redesign the service for everyone.
cards.softwareNote: The same moves apply to a software product: pick a narrow group of users, onboard each one yourself, offer a time-limited founding price for regular feedback, and call every early user who cancels.

cards.title: Your first ten customers come from four decisions.
body: Each choice in Dana's story matches an idea from this unit:
list: **Who first:** a narrow group with the same pain (Your first 10 customers)
**How to reach them:** personal, warm, and in their world (Cold outreach)
**What to charge:** a real price, with a discount that buys feedback and referrals (Design partners, Pricing your first deals)
**When they leave:** ask why before you change anything (Learning from lost deals)
cards.callout: **Try it today:** write down the one group you'd sell to first, and the place where you could meet five of them this week.
